name: datasette
recipe: N/A — no viable lane. Datasette is a Python ASGI application served by uvicorn/hypercorn over a bound TCP listener; its product is the HTTP server itself. Python is already LIVE in-sandbox, but a wasm32-wasi guest under wasmtime cannot bind/listen on a socket (network-as-purpose), so the server cannot run. Datasette Lite (Pyodide) only "works" because a browser + service worker intercept fetch — browser dependency, also disqualifying. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm exists; it's pure-Python-on-Pyodide, not a standalone CLI.
smoke: N/A — cannot smoke-test; no in-sandbox artifact possible. (A socket-bound HTTP server cannot be started under WASI without fork/exec/network.)
blocker: Long-running HTTP server is the product; WASI under wasmtime cannot bind/listen on a TCP socket (network-as-purpose). Browser-only path (Datasette Lite via Pyodide + service-worker fetch interception) is browser-dependent. Both disqualifying.

name: weasyprint
recipe: No viable recipe. WeasyPrint is Python but NOT pure-Python (lane D excluded): its core dependency `cffi >=0.6` (pyproject.toml) exists solely to dlopen native shared libraries at runtime via weasyprint/text/ffi.py — libgobject-2.0, libpango-1.0, libpangoft2-1.0, libharfbuzz(+subset), libfontconfig. These provide all text layout/shaping/font enumeration; WeasyPrint cannot run a single layout without them. cffi dynamic-binding + native .so/.dylib loading is impossible under wasm32-wasi/wasmtime (no native dynamic linker, no native Pango/HarfBuzz/Fontconfig objects in sandbox). Pyodide path also fails: Pyodide targets emscripten (not plain wasm32-wasi under wasmtime), and crucially ships NO weasyprint package precisely because cffi+Pango can't be provided. The 2021 cairo->pydyf switch only removed the cairo drawing backend; the Pango/HarfBuzz/Fontconfig text stack via cffi remains and is the blocker. Even though freetype+harfbuzz are LIVE here, that does not help: WeasyPrint binds to them through cffi's native dlopen ABI, not a wasm-linked lib, and additionally requires Pango+GObject+Fontconfig which are not present and are themselves cffi-dlopen'd C libraries.
smoke:
If hypothetically built: `python -c "import weasyprint; weasyprint.HTML(string='

hi

').write_pdf('/out.pdf')"` then check /out.pdf starts with %PDF and renders one page. In practice this fails at import time: weasyprint/text/ffi.py calls ffi.dlopen('libgobject-2.0...') which raises OSError (cannot load native shared library) under wasm32-wasi.
blocker: Core dep cffi dlopen's native Pango/HarfBuzz/Fontconfig/GObject shared libraries (weasyprint/text/ffi.py) for all text layout — native dynamic linking unavailable under wasm32-wasi/wasmtime; not pure-Python; Pyodide ships no weasyprint package for this exact reason.

name: yt-dlp
recipe: N/A — does not qualify for any lane. Lane D (pure-Python pip) fails on two grounds: (1) yt-dlp's entire purpose IS network egress to thousands of arbitrary remote hosts — that is network-as-purpose, explicitly disqualifying. (2) It fork-execs ffmpeg/ffprobe for muxing/post-processing and shells out to a JS runtime (deno/node/bun/QuickJS via yt-dlp-ejs) to solve YouTube nsig/JS challenges — both are fork-exec of native subprocesses, disqualifying. The extractor logic alone is pure Python and would import under the LIVE python (Pyodide-style), but the extractors are useless without the brokered net + ffmpeg subprocess + JS-challenge engine that constitute the actual function. Not a self-contained computation; it is an I/O orchestration tool.
smoke: No valid in-sandbox smoke exists. The only thing that would "run" (python -c "import yt_dlp; print(yt_dlp.version.__version__)") proves nothing — any real extraction (yt-dlp URL) immediately requires outbound HTTP to the target host + ffmpeg subprocess, neither available in the no-net/no-fork sandbox, so it fails at the first network call.
blocker: Network-as-purpose: yt-dlp's sole function is HTTP egress to thousands of arbitrary external hosts. Compounded by fork-exec dependencies (ffmpeg/ffprobe for muxing; a native JS runtime for YouTube JS-challenge solving). All three are explicitly disqualifying for the in-sandbox model. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi target exists (only native .exe/Linux/macOS binaries + source dist).

name: ssh / scp (OpenSSH)
recipe: No viable lane. OpenSSH is a C codebase whose purpose is the network: the ssh client opens a raw outbound TCP socket and speaks the SSH transport protocol over it. wasip1 exposes no outbound TCP connect(), so the program's reason-to-exist (network-as-purpose) is unmet in-sandbox. Even brokering TCP via a host Dock import does not rescue it: OpenSSH additionally relies on fork()/exec() (forks a child per connection, execs the user's login shell / scp / sftp-server / ssh-askpass), PTY allocation (openpty/forkpty), full POSIX signal handling, and privilege separation via fork()+setuid — none of which exist under wasm32-wasi/wasmtime. The crypto core (cipher/kex/mac) is pure-compute and would be fine, but it is a small fraction of the program and cannot be shipped as a standalone ssh/scp binary. Existing WASM SSH efforts (Google WASSH, hullarb/ssheasy) are all browser-bound: they rely on a JS host to proxy WebSocket/relay sockets and a DOM terminal — not a standalone wasm32-wasi module under wasmtime. No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists.
smoke: N/A — cannot build/run. If forced to attempt: `clang --target=wasm32-wasi` over OpenSSH would fail/abort at link or runtime on missing connect()/socket(), fork(), forkpty(), and sigaction; `wasmtime ssh user@host` could never open the TCP channel that is the program's sole function.
blocker: Network-as-purpose: ssh/scp exist solely to open a raw outbound TCP socket and run the SSH protocol over it, which wasip1 cannot do. Compounded by hard dependence on fork/exec (per-connection child + user shell + scp/sftp/ssh-askpass), PTY allocation, signals, and fork-based privilege separation — all absent in wasm32-wasi. Crypto is fine but is not the binary. Prior WASM SSH ports are browser+JS-socket only, not standalone wasmtime modules.

name: GnuTLS
recipe: Lane B (self-contained C), but heavy multi-tarball with a configure cascade. Deps needed as :deps tarballs: GMP (gmplib.org), nettle+hogweed (which depends on GMP), libtasn1 (GnuTLS bundles a copy via --with-included-libtasn1), libunistring (--with-included-unistring), and p11-kit MUST be dropped (--without-p11-kit; it pulls dlopen/PKCS#11 module loading = fork/dlopen-shaped, not sandbox-friendly). Build order: GMP first with --disable-assembly (pure-C mpn fallback path exists and works under wasm32; the x86-64 .asm is bypassed), then nettle with --disable-assembly --disable-fat (nettle's fat-library asm selection is config-time codegen and must be turned off), then GnuTLS configured --without-p11-kit --without-idn --disable-doc --disable-tools --with-included-libtasn1 --with-included-unistring. Each component is an autotools project emitting config.h via feature-detection, so all four configures must be pre-run on a host and the generated config headers + Makefile-derived source lists checked in as pregenerated artifacts (config-substitution), then compiled with :compile_only / :include_only against wasi-sdk libc. No codegen tools (m4/gawk for nettle's asm, gperf) run in-sandbox. Disable getrandom-as-syscall path: GnuTLS/nettle entropy must be wired to WASI random_get (wasi-libc provides getentropy), not /dev/urandom fork.
smoke: In-sandbox under wasmtime, run a tiny C driver linking the built libgnutls: call gnutls_global_init(); print gnutls_check_version(NULL) (expect "3.8.x"); then exercise pure-compute crypto with no network: gnutls_hash_fast(GNUTLS_DIG_SHA256, "abc", 3, out) and assert the digest == ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad. This proves nettle/GMP/tasn1 linked and the ASN.1+hash paths run without any socket/fork. (A full handshake needs an in-memory BIO via gnutls_transport_set_push/pull_function over two buffers — no real sockets — but the hash+version smoke is the minimal go/no-go.)
blocker: Multi-tarball configure cascade (GnuTLS + nettle + GMP + libtasn1 + libunistring), each an autotools project whose config.h and source lists are generated by host-side configure/m4 — not a pregenerated source drop, so it violates Lane B's no-configure rule unless all four configures are pre-run on a host and the headers checked in. nettle's asm is config-time fat-library codegen (must --disable-assembly --disable-fat); GMP asm likewise disabled (C fallback OK). p11-kit must be dropped (dlopen/PKCS#11 module loading). This is the heaviest port in the set and is fully obviated by mbedtls, which is already LIVE and gives in-sandbox TLS with zero of this dep web.

name: Jupyter
recipe: None viable. Jupyter is a client/server protocol app, not a single computational binary. Architecture: Tornado HTTP/WebSocket server (jupyter_server) + ZMQ-based kernels (pyzmq, 5 sockets per kernel) + browser web UI. Kernel management is fork-exec of separate processes; kernel<->server messaging is ZMQ network/IPC sockets; serving is network-as-purpose; UI is a browser. The only wasm variant, JupyterLite, is emscripten + JS running IN-BROWSER (Pyodide kernel + ServiceWorker shim) -- explicitly NOT a plain wasm32-wasi .wasm under wasmtime (excluded from Lane A). The jupyter glue is pure-Python but its load-bearing deps (pyzmq, tornado) are C-ext networking libs requiring real sockets + fork-exec. Python interpreter itself is already LIVE in-sandbox, but Jupyter-the-app cannot run there.
smoke: N/A -- impossible. (If a kernel were somehow standalone, smoke would be: echo execute_request over the ZMQ shell socket and expect an iopub execute_result -- but ZMQ sockets + fork-exec kernel spawn are forbidden in-sandbox.)
blocker: fork-exec (kernel process spawning) + network-as-purpose (Tornado server + ZMQ inter-process sockets) + browser web UI. Only wasm path (JupyterLite) is emscripten/JS-in-browser, not wasm32-wasi/wasmtime. No prebuilt plain .wasm, no self-contained C/C++ computational core, no bare Rust crate.

name: TeX Live
recipe: No viable lane. Lane A: no prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm exists — every TeX-to-WASM build (BusyTeX, SwiftLaTeX, TeXLive.js, TeXlyre/busytex 2026) is an EMSCRIPTEN build emitting a .wasm + .js glue pair (MEMFS, browser/Node FS shims, worker scripts), not a standalone wasm32-wasi binary runnable under wasmtime; none use wasi-sdk. Lane B: 'TeX Live' as scoped is the full multi-GB distribution, not a single C/C++ tarball — it is thousands of packages + font trees (texmf) + a Perl-driven tooling layer (tlmgr, mktexlsr, latexmk, kpathsea index generation). The C engine (pdftex/web2c) alone is C, but the distribution deliverable requires a Perl runtime (does not compile to wasm here) and multi-GB texmf provisioning at build/run time. Lanes C/D N/A (not Rust/Python/JS).
smoke: N/A — cannot run. Were a wasi pdftex.wasm to exist, smoke would be: echo '\documentclass{article}\begin{document}hi\end{document}' > t.tex; wasmtime run --dir=. pdftex.wasm t.tex; test -f t.pdf. But it requires a populated texmf tree (kpathsea path lookup) which is the multi-GB provisioning blocker, and no wasi .wasm exists to run.
blocker: No standalone wasm32-wasi build exists — all TeX-to-WASM is Emscripten+JS-glue (browser/MEMFS), not wasmtime-runnable. Beyond the engine, 'TeX Live' is a multi-GB distribution gated on a Perl tooling layer (tlmgr/mktexlsr, won't compile to wasm) and multi-GB texmf font/package provisioning — neither is a self-contained C/C++ compile lane.

name: Objective-C
smoke: N/A — cannot stand up a usable Objective-C runtime in-sandbox. (If a runtime existed, the smoke would be: compile `@interface Greeter:NSObject` + `[g greet]` with clang.wasm against a wasm libobjc, run under wasmtime, expect "hello" on stdout. No such runtime exists.)
blocker: clang.wasm compiles the ObjC frontend (AOT, no JIT), but the LANGUAGE is inert without an ObjC runtime. Apple's libobjc + Foundation are macOS/iOS-only and closed. The portable runtime, GNUstep libobjc2, implements objc_msgSend as hand-written per-arch ASSEMBLY (x86-64/aarch64/arm/riscv64) — a tail-call trampoline jumping to a runtime-resolved IMP — and has NO wasm32 backend; wasm's structured control flow + typed-table indirect calls make a drop-in trampoline non-trivial. No public libobjc2 wasm port exists. Foundation (gnustep-base) is a large autotools/configure tree with net+fs assumptions, not a self-contained tarball (fails Lane B). Only documented ObjC->wasm (Apple iWork) used a proprietary internal ObjC runtime+Foundation, not reproducible. Frontend-compiles != runnable language. Not Rust/Python/JS. No Lane fits.

name: Parcel
recipe: No viable recipe. Parcel v2 is a Node.js bundler: its core (@parcel/rust) ships only as platform-specific native .node N-API addons (no wasm32-wasi build published), its SWC transformer is also a native addon, and its runtime architecture depends on Node worker_threads + child-process fork for parallelism plus a native filesystem/watcher layer. Lane A: no prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (only Darwin/Linux/Win native binaries). Lane B: N/A (Rust+JS, not C/C++). Lane C: the Rust core is large, proc-macro-heavy (napi-rs + serde derive), N-API-bound rather than a standalone CLI -> mrustc ~1.74 cannot build it. Lane D: the JS layer is a thin orchestrator delegating to native addons and spawning worker threads/forks -> running it on QuickJS yields no functional bundler and still requires native-threads + fork-exec.
smoke: N/A - cannot build. If a wasm32-wasi artifact ever existed: `wasmtime parcel.wasm build index.html` over a tiny fixture and diff dist/ output. No such artifact is shippable today.
blocker: Core is native .node N-API addons (no wasm32-wasi build); architecture requires Node worker_threads + fork-exec for parallelism and native fs/watcher. Native-threads + fork-exec + native-addon ABI are all out of reach for standalone wasm32-wasi under wasmtime. Rust core too large/proc-macro/N-API for mrustc; JS-on-QuickJS gives no real bundler since all work lives in native code.

name: Farm
recipe: No recipe. Farm ships as a NAPI-RS native addon (@farmfe/core loads a prebuilt .node binary per platform via @farmfe/core-{os}-{arch} packages). The Rust core is compiled to a native Node addon, not wasm32-wasi. It depends on rayon native OS-thread parallelism, a native persistent disk cache, an embedded dev-server (HTTP/WS as the purpose), and a JS plugin bridge over N-API into a host Node process. None of these survive standalone wasm32-wasi under wasmtime: no native threads, no fork-exec, no N-API/Node embedding, no networked dev-server. There is no wasm build today; producing one would require rewriting threading (rayon->single-thread), replacing N-API with a different host seam, and dropping the dev-server — i.e. a from-scratch port, not a packaging job. Out of scope for Lane A (no prebuilt plain wasm), B (Rust not C/C++), C (huge multi-crate workspace + swc + proc-macros + edition2024 -> mrustc-impossible), and D (it is the native engine, not the JS layer).
smoke: N/A — nothing to build. If forced: `npm pack @farmfe/core` and inspect deps -> resolves to @farmfe/core-darwin-arm64 etc. shipping a `*.node` native binary, with zero `*.wasm` artifact; confirms native-addon-only distribution.
blocker: NAPI-RS native Node addon (.node), not wasm: requires rayon native threads + Node N-API host embedding + native disk cache + a networked dev-server as its purpose. fork-exec/native-threads/network-as-purpose/Node-embedding all unsupported under standalone wasm32-wasi on wasmtime. No wasm build exists; a port is a full rewrite.

name: Mako
recipe: No viable recipe. Mako (@umijs/mako, latest 0.11.15) ships ONLY as per-platform napi native binaries (optionalDependencies: @umijs/mako-darwin-arm64, -linux-x64-gnu, -linux-x64-musl, -win32-x64-msvc, etc.). No wasm artifact, no wasm32-wasi target. Lane A fails (no prebuilt .wasm). Lane B N/A (Rust, not C/C++). Lane C (mrustc ~1.74) impossible: large multi-crate SWC-based workspace, proc-macro-heavy (napi-rs, serde derive), native-thread-dependent (rayon/tokio worker pools), edition2021+. Lane D N/A (not Python/JS).
smoke: N/A — nothing to build. If a wasm port ever existed: `wasmtime mako.wasm build --config-file mako.config.json` against a trivial entry.ts producing dist/index.js. Not achievable.
blocker: Native-threads-as-purpose (rayon/tokio multi-threaded bundling), napi native Node binding, and native fs-watching (notify). No wasm artifact exists and porting requires shimming threads/fs/napi — all impossible-class for in-sandbox wasm32-wasi under wasmtime. mrustc cannot compile the proc-macro-heavy SWC workspace.

name: TDengine
recipe: None viable. TDengine is the clustered taosd daemon: its purpose IS network serving (TCP/UDP cluster RPC, epoll event loops, mnode/vnode coordination), plus per-vnode native pthreads and raw block disk IO. Lane A: no prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (search returned only unrelated TiDB/TDLib hits). Lane B: the C core cannot run single-threaded, networkless, or fork-free; the TSDB storage engine is not shipped as a standalone embeddable library (only reachable via the daemon). Lanes C/D: N/A (C project, not Rust/Python/JS).
smoke: N/A — no standalone embeddable artifact to exercise. Daemon requires sockets + native threads + epoll at startup, which the sandbox forbids; nothing runnable below the network boundary.
blocker: Network-as-purpose (cluster RPC/epoll) + native pthreads per vnode + raw disk IO; no prebuilt wasm and no standalone storage-engine library to isolate.

name: DoltDB
recipe: No viable lane. Dolt is written in Go (~hundreds of thousands of LOC: go-mysql-server engine = MySQL parser + query planner + analyzer, the noms/prolly Merkle-DAG storage layer, a SQL server, and a sprawling go.mod dependency tree). The four lanes here are: A=prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm, B=self-contained C/C++ via the compile toolchain, C=bare Rust crate via mrustc, D=pure-Python/JS. Go fits NONE of them — there is no Go compiler in the in-sandbox toolchain (clang/mrustc/zig/yaegi/quickjs only), and Go cannot be compiled by any of those. The only Go-to-wasm path is the upstream `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm` toolchain, which (a) we do not host, and (b) yields a multi-MB bundle carrying Go's GC + goroutine scheduler that assumes native-thread-like async and is unsuited to a single-threaded was32-wasi CLI. Dolt's own team reached the same conclusion: the Go-to-WASM route was deemed impractical, so they shipped DoltLite — a fork that vendors SQLite's C ext/wasm build instead. SQLite is ALREADY LIVE in this sandbox (sqlite3), so the Git-versioned-SQL value would have to come from porting DoltLite's C layer separately, not from Dolt itself.
smoke: N/A — cannot build. If a Go toolchain existed: `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build ./cmd/dolt && wasmtime dolt.wasm sql -q "select 1"` — but no Go compiler is in-sandbox and the resulting binary's threaded GC runtime is incompatible with the single-threaded wasm32-wasi CLI target.
blocker: Written in Go; no Go compiler in the in-sandbox toolchain (clang/mrustc/zig/yaegi/quickjs only) and Go is not buildable by any of them. The only Go->wasm path (GOOS=wasip1) is unhosted and ships a multi-MB GC+goroutine-scheduler runtime unfit for single-threaded wasm32-wasi. Upstream itself abandoned the Go-to-WASM route in favor of DoltLite (C/SQLite). Note: SQLite is already LIVE.

name: Crystal
recipe: N/A — no viable lane. Crystal is a compiled language whose toolchain (crystal compiler) is built on native LLVM and requires wasm-ld at link time; it is not a self-contained C/C++ library (rules out Lane B). There is no prebuilt standalone plain wasm32-wasi .wasm of the Crystal compiler or runtime (rules out Lane A). It is not a Rust crate (C) nor pure-Python/JS (D). Even producing a Crystal *program* as wasm requires: native LLVM codegen + wasm-ld, libc+libpcre cross-compiled to wasi, and the Boehm GC (libgc) patched to run under wasm via fiber stack unwind/rewind. The resulting runtime depends on exception-handling and GC stack-inspection machinery that is experimental/incomplete.
smoke: N/A — cannot run. If a Crystal-produced .wasm were obtained, smoke would be: wasmtime hello.wasm printing a string. But the compiler itself cannot run in-sandbox (no native LLVM/wasm-ld in sandbox), so even building such a .wasm is out of scope here.
blocker: No prebuilt standalone wasm32-wasi Crystal compiler/runtime exists, and Crystal is not a buildable self-contained C/C++ library — its toolchain is native LLVM + wasm-ld (codegen toolchain, excluded). wasm support is experimental/incomplete: GC (Boehm libgc) needs fiber stack unwind/rewind hacks, exception handling unfinished, fibers need Binaryen Asyncify wrapping, stack traces infeasible, threads/Process/sockets unsupported under WASI. Most of stdlib (IO, signals, sockets, Process, GC, concurrency, OpenSSL, Zlib) does not work. No way to bring Crystal in as a standalone in-sandbox wasm.

name: Racket
recipe: No viable lane. Racket CS runs on Chez Scheme native-code compiler, JIT-shaped, no standalone wasm32-wasi. All Racket-on-wasm work is experimental, subset, or browser/JS-targeted. No prebuilt wasm.
smoke: racket prints 3 for one plus two, but no wasm32-wasi binary exists
blocker: Chez Scheme native-code/JIT-shaped codegen incompatible with jitless wasm32-wasi; no prebuilt wasm; emscripten fallback is browser/JS-pair

name: Vale
blocker: Scala frontend needs a JVM with no wasm32-wasi JVM. C++ backend bound to native LLVM13 codegen. Multi-stage fork-exec toolchain, no prebuilt wasm. JIT and fork-exec both disqualify.
smoke: None possible; no standalone wasm32-wasi module exists. JVM frontend plus native LLVM13 backend means nothing runs as a single wasm under wasmtime.
recipe: No lane fits. Vale compiler is Scala frontend 54.8 percent needing JVM plus C++ backend 42.1 percent bound to native LLVM13. A: no prebuilt wasm32-wasi wasm. B: not self-contained C or C++ since Scala JVM frontend and LLVM-as-library backend. C: not Rust. D: not pure Python or QuickJS JS. Only frontend-to-wasm path is JVM-in-wasm jit-bound none packaged, or a nonexistent Scala.js or TeaVM port.

name: Unison
recipe: No viable lane. ucm (Unison Codebase Manager = the runtime + bytecode interpreter) is a Haskell/GHC program distributed only as native binaries (macOS/Linux/Windows). No wasm32-wasi build exists (Lane A fails: no prebuilt .wasm, none is emscripten/js either). Not C/C++ (Lane B n/a), not Rust (Lane C n/a), not Python/JS (Lane D n/a). Building ucm would require cross-compiling a large multi-package Haskell project via GHC's experimental wasm backend pulling the full GHC RTS — a full-compile effort explicitly out of scope, and the GHC RTS relies on green-thread scheduling/native runtime services that do not map to standalone wasm32-wasi. Unison's actual value (content-addressed code-as-hash distributed over a network with a backing codebase store / SQLite + network sync) is network-as-purpose, which is disqualifying on its own.
smoke: N/A — nothing to build. If a hypothetical static `ucm` wasm existed: `ucm --help` then `echo 'x = 1 + 1' | ucm run.compiled` to evaluate one term offline. Not attemptable: no wasm artifact and network-backed runtime.
blocker: Haskell/GHC-RTS runtime (no wasm32-wasi build; needs green threads/native runtime) plus network-as-purpose (distributed code-as-hash + network codebase sync). Not C/Rust/Python/JS; building = full GHC cross-compile, out of scope.

name: Curry
recipe: No viable lane. Curry has no standalone compiler/runtime — every implementation bootstraps on a heavyweight host language toolchain that is itself unavailable as wasm32-wasi: KiCS2 compiles Curry->Haskell and requires GHC; PAKCS compiles Curry->Prolog and requires SWI-Prolog (only an emscripten/JS wasm pair exists, not a standalone wasi binary); Curry2Go compiles Curry->Go and requires the native Go toolchain plus a parallel fair search strategy. The curry-frontend parser is written in Haskell. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm (Lane A absent). Not self-contained C/C++ (Lane B), not a bare Rust crate (Lane C), not pure-Python/JS (Lane D). Building it would require first standing up GHC, SWI-Prolog, or Go inside the sandbox.
smoke: N/A — cannot build. If a wasm32-wasi curry binary existed: echo 'main = putStrLn "ok"' > t.curry && wasmtime curry.wasm :load t :eval main :quit  (expect "ok").
blocker: All Curry systems require a host toolchain unavailable/unsuitable for wasm32-wasi under wasmtime: KiCS2 needs GHC-Haskell, PAKCS needs SWI-Prolog (only emscripten/JS wasm exists), Curry2Go needs native Go + native-thread parallel fair search. No standalone wasm binary; runtimes rely on native threads and fork-style nondeterministic search. Not C/C++, Rust-crate, Python, or JS — no lane applies.

name: Sather
recipe: N/A — no viable lane. Sather is an abandoned GNU research language (last real release ~1.x in the late 1990s). (A) No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists anywhere — never targeted wasm. (B) Not a self-contained C/C++ library: the compiler is a bootstrapped Sather/C toolchain with an autoconf/configure build that emits C and depends on its own runtime + Boehm GC; it's a code-generating compiler, not a config-substitution-friendly C lib, and the build is known-broken/crumbling. (C) Not a Rust crate. (D) Not pure-Python/JS. The 'emitted C compiles via our C lane' angle is moot because you first need a working Sather compiler to emit that C, and that compiler can't be built standalone in-sandbox (configure + self-hosting bootstrap).
smoke: N/A — nothing to smoke-test; no buildable/runnable artifact reachable in-sandbox.
blocker: No prebuilt wasm; compiler is a self-hosting Sather/C bootstrap with a broken autoconf/configure + codegen build needing Boehm GC and its own runtime — not a self-contained C library and not buildable standalone in-sandbox. Lane B excluded by codegen/configure requirement; no Rust/Python/JS form exists.
